purpose: Coordinate the next UIX Apps development sprint across UX, cinematic systems, polyglot code, quality, and server publication.

polyglotLanguageGrowth.targetDirection: Preserve and expand governed software-language coverage when each new lane has a clear product, governance, or handoff role.
promotionRules: Every new language lane must update the software-language matrix, polyglot manifest, starter source file, checker marker, server handoff requirement, and docs.
Reference lanes stay dependency-free until a runtime need is explicit.
Prefer small contracts, adapters, readiness signals, schemas, or handoff files over new package managers or compilers.
Keep all language-lane changes reversible, reviewable, and compatible with low-power validation.

lanes.label: UX Apps module
lanes.focus: Keep archive intelligence, cinematic program, and zip promotion lab visible in the canonical repo.
lanes.nextAction: Promote one reviewed zip insight into the UX Apps module per sprint.

lanes.label: Cinematic UI
lanes.focus: Run a restrained canvas depth layer inside the development cockpit without increasing cognitive load.
lanes.nextAction: Tune cinematic-depth settings after visual smoke checks.

lanes.label: Polyglot branch
lanes.focus: Keep at least 26 software languages represented as governed starter lanes rather than scattered experiments.
lanes.qualitySignal: npm run check:software-languages && npm run check:polyglot-foundation
lanes.nextAction: Expand language lanes only when the automation policy can add manifest, checker, handoff, docs, and rollback-safe starter coverage together.

lanes.label: Server delivery
lanes.focus: Preserve upload-ready source bundles until GitHub/server credentials are configured.
lanes.nextAction: Configure UIX_UPLOAD_HOST, UIX_UPLOAD_USER, and UIX_UPLOAD_PATH when the server target is known.

decisionSlots.question: Which calm cinematic surface should be promoted first?
Which real server should receive the generated bundle?
